newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MILLWALL SACK MANAGER, PUT 12 PLAYERS UP FOR SALE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILLWALL SACK MANAGER, PUT 12 PLAYERS UP FOR SALE.

text.p: London club Millwall sacked their manager Jimmy Nicholl and chief executive Graham Hortop on Monday and transfer-listed 12 players in a drastic 1.5 million pound ($2.4 million) cost-cutting exercise.
They also asked all remaining staff and players to take a 10 percent cut in wages.
Manager Jimmy Nicholl, a former Northern Ireland international who had been manager since February 1996 was replaced by John Docherty, back at the club he took into the top flight in 1988.

Millwall have been relegated twice since then and have accumulated debts of around 10 million pounds ($16.3 million). Trading in their shares was suspended on the London stock exchange last month and the club was handed over to administrators.

"These cuts were always seen as an integral part of the way forward," the administrators said on Monday. "It's a very painful but necessary process... It was our view that changes needed to be made in both areas to stimulate success both on and off the field.''

It was a busy day for English league clubs on Monday with Millwall's division two rivals Bournemouth winning their first battle to stay afloat when they won a High Court adjournment against a winding-up order.
The cash-strapped club now has three weeks to attract new investment and present its case for survival to the English Football League.

Meanwhile first division Southend suspended manager Ronnie Whelan and dismissed his assistant Theo Foley after the two men were both ordered out of the dugout during their team's 3-0 defeat at Manchester City on Saturday.

Whelan, the former Liverpool player who has been at Southend since July 1995, has been suspended on full pay pending the referee's report into the incident which followed a tackle by City's Georgian midfielder Georgi Kinkladze on Southend's Phil Gridelet.
